correctness.rationale: Conjugate E to e11 by choosing bases of its free image and kernel. The complementary diagonal corners are already in the scalar-inclusive algebra, and multiplication on the left and right by E and I−E isolates the two off-diagonal entries of F. The candidate submodule is closed under multiplication, so the off-diagonal ideals are precisely bR and cR and the additive index exponent is ν(b)+ν(c). Trace one and determinant zero are necessary and sufficient for these idempotents, using Cayley–Hamilton and residue rank. For bc in the maximal ideal, the two simple residue roots 0 and 1 each lift once at each quotient: the correction in the next layer solves a linear equation with unit derivative, even in characteristic two. For bc a unit, exactly (q−2)q^(m−1) choices of t and (q−1)q^(m−1) choices of b determine c. There are q^(m−1)(q+1) image lines (count unimodular vectors modulo units), each with q^m complementary kernels (graphs of maps from a fixed complement). This gives the ordered-pair factor and the product inclusion order, reversed in each valuation. The only omitted pair is the unit–unit pair for q=2. Below m the finite coefficients match the limiting geometric convolution (with adjusted mass at zero); its geometric tail is 2((q−1)m+q)/((q+1)q^m), bounding total variation. Differentiating the limiting series gives 4q/(q²−1), and evaluating B_m at q gives q^(m−1)[m(q−1)+q], yielding the critical expectation. This is a proof for arbitrary residue-field size and either characteristic, not inference from the frozen nine-ring output; the uploaded checker was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: Instead of a generation yes/no test, the theorem quantifies every attainable defect by a pair of Peirce ideals and gives its full frequency. The resulting tight log-index law versus quadratic growth of the actual mean index is a substantive distinction for a natural small-matrix generating system; the index alone is not an invariant that distinguishes both ideals or conjugacy classes.
